claims.title: Duklja wins independence from Byzantium
claims.summary: Stefan Vojislav led a revolt that freed the principality of Duklja from Byzantine control and established the Vojislavljevic dynasty, the first medieval state on the territory of Montenegro.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Montenegro: A mountain stronghold that defied an empire, lost its crown to a union, and won back its statehood by a single percentage point.", terralore.co/country/MNE/chronicle#ev-1042-duklja-wins-independence-from-byzantium, claim TL:MNE:event:1042:duklja-wins-independence-from-byzantium, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mihailo crowned king of Duklja
claims.summary: Mihailo of Duklja became the first ruler of the region to bear the royal title, the crown bestowed on him by Pope Gregory VII, marking Duklja's standing among Christian states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Montenegro: A mountain stronghold that defied an empire, lost its crown to a union, and won back its statehood by a single percentage point.", terralore.co/country/MNE/chronicle#ev-1077-mihailo-crowned-king-of-duklja, claim TL:MNE:event:1077:mihailo-crowned-king-of-duklja, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Principality of Zeta under the Balsic
claims.summary: After the fall of the Serbian Empire an independent Zeta emerged, ruled by the House of Balsic and then from 1431 by the House of Crnojevic, under whom the name Montenegro came into use.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Montenegro: A mountain stronghold that defied an empire, lost its crown to a union, and won back its statehood by a single percentage point.", terralore.co/country/MNE/chronicle#ev-1356-principality-of-zeta-under-the-balsic, claim TL:MNE:event:1356:principality-of-zeta-under-the-balsic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Oktoih and the Crnojevic printing press
claims.summary: Djurdje Crnojevic founded the first South Slavic printing house at Cetinje, which produced the Oktoih, the first Cyrillic book printed in southeastern Europe, before closing around 1496 amid the Ottoman advance.

sources.label: History of the Crnojevic printing house and the Oktoih

claims.title: Rise of the theocratic Prince-Bishopric
claims.summary: Authority over the free Montenegrin highlands passed to the Orthodox bishops of Cetinje, who combined spiritual and temporal power as vladikas in a theocratic state that renounced Ottoman overlordship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Montenegro: A mountain stronghold that defied an empire, lost its crown to a union, and won back its statehood by a single percentage point.", terralore.co/country/MNE/chronicle#ev-1516-rise-of-the-theocratic-prince-bishopric, claim TL:MNE:event:1516:rise-of-the-theocratic-prince-bishopric, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Petrovic-Njegos dynasty established
claims.summary: Metropolitan Danilo Petrovic-Njegos secured the right to name his successor, founding the hereditary Petrovic-Njegos line of prince-bishops that ruled Montenegro until 1918, the title passing from uncle to nephew.

sources.label: Danilo I, first prince-bishop of the Petrovic-Njegos dynasty

claims.title: Rule of Petar II Petrovic-Njegos
claims.summary: The poet-prince Petar II strengthened the state, founded schools and reformed taxation, and wrote The Mountain Wreath, becoming Montenegro's most celebrated cultural figure.

sources.label: Peter II (Petar II Petrovic-Njegos), prince-bishop of Montenegro

claims.title: Publication of The Mountain Wreath
claims.summary: Njegos published Gorski vijenac (The Mountain Wreath), a dramatic epic in verse set in eighteenth-century Montenegro that became a defining work of the national literature.

sources.label: Peter II (Petar II Petrovic-Njegos), prince-bishop of Montenegro

claims.title: Montenegro becomes a secular principality
claims.summary: Danilo renounced the office of prince-bishop, married and proclaimed himself prince, ending the theocracy; his 1855 code gave the principality its first modern legal framework.

sources.label: Danilo II, prince-bishop and first secular prince of Montenegro

claims.title: Independence recognised at the Congress of Berlin
claims.summary: The Treaty of Berlin recognised Montenegro's independence under Article XXVI, ending Ottoman suzerainty, and under Article XXIX enlarged the state and granted it the port of Antivari (Bar).

sources.label: Treaty of Berlin (1878), Articles XXVI-XXXIII on Montenegro
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian (FRUS 1878)

sources.label: Congress of Berlin and recognition of Montenegro, 1878

claims.title: First Montenegrin constitution
claims.summary: Prince Nikola I granted Montenegro its first constitution, establishing an assembly and modern institutions as the principality consolidated its recognised statehood.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Montenegro: A mountain stronghold that defied an empire, lost its crown to a union, and won back its statehood by a single percentage point.", terralore.co/country/MNE/chronicle#ev-1905-first-montenegrin-constitution, claim TL:MNE:event:1905:first-montenegrin-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Montenegro proclaimed a kingdom
claims.summary: On the fiftieth anniversary of his reign, Prince Nikola I proclaimed Montenegro a kingdom and assumed the title of king, the last monarchy created in the Balkans.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Montenegro: A mountain stronghold that defied an empire, lost its crown to a union, and won back its statehood by a single percentage point.", terralore.co/country/MNE/chronicle#ev-1910-montenegro-proclaimed-a-kingdom, claim TL:MNE:event:1910:montenegro-proclaimed-a-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Balkan Wars
claims.summary: Montenegro joined Serbia, Bulgaria and Greece in the First Balkan War against the Ottoman Empire and besieged Scutari, but was forced by the Great Powers to give up the captured city.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Montenegro: A mountain stronghold that defied an empire, lost its crown to a union, and won back its statehood by a single percentage point.", terralore.co/country/MNE/chronicle#ev-1912-the-balkan-wars, claim TL:MNE:event:1912:the-balkan-wars, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Mojkovac and Austro-Hungarian occupation
claims.summary: The Montenegrin army won the Battle of Mojkovac (7-8 January 1916) to cover the Serbian retreat, but the kingdom was overrun and occupied by Austria-Hungary, and King Nikola I fled into exile.

claims.title: The Podgorica Assembly
claims.summary: An assembly in Podgorica deposed King Nikola I and the Petrovic-Njegos dynasty and proclaimed the unconditional union of Montenegro with Serbia in the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes.

sources.label: Montenegro (First World War)

claims.title: The Christmas Uprising and the Greens-Whites split
claims.summary: Pro-independence 'Greens' rose against the union proclaimed at Podgorica but were defeated by the unionist 'Whites', a schism over Montenegro's statehood that endured for generations.

sources.label: Montenegro (First World War)

claims.title: Socialist Republic of Montenegro
claims.summary: After wartime occupation and partisan resistance, Montenegro became one of the six federal republics of socialist Yugoslavia, with its capital at Titograd, today's Podgorica.

claims.title: Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
claims.summary: As the other republics broke away, Montenegro joined Serbia in forming the rump Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, remaining bound to Belgrade through the wars and sanctions of the 1990s.

claims.title: Unilateral adoption of the euro
claims.summary: Montenegro made the euro its sole legal tender from March 2002, a unilateral euroisation undertaken without European Central Bank agreement that distanced its economy from Serbia's.

sources.label: Euroisation: Montenegro's adoption of the Deutsche Mark and then the euro (sole legal tender from March 2002)

claims.title: State Union of Serbia and Montenegro
claims.summary: European mediation transformed the federation into the loose State Union of Serbia and Montenegro, whose Constitutional Charter allowed either republic to hold an independence referendum after three years.

claims.title: Independence referendum
claims.summary: On a turnout above 86 percent, 55.5 percent of voters chose independence, narrowly passing the EU-set 55 percent threshold; the OSCE/ODIHR found the vote met international standards.

claims.title: Restoration of independence
claims.summary: The parliament in Podgorica formally declared Montenegro an independent sovereign state, recognised by Serbia, restoring the statehood lost at the Podgorica Assembly of 1918.

claims.summary: Montenegro and Kosovo signed a demarcation of their 79-kilometre border in 2015; fiercely contested in Kosovo, it was finally ratified by Pristina's parliament in March 2018.

claims.summary: Montenegro became NATO's twenty-ninth member, depositing its instrument of accession in Washington, despite strong Russian opposition and a divided domestic public.
